events.text: Through the thread you see what your avatar sees: the ruin of a domain whose god was forgotten, its temple upside down in the Star River, steps going down into the current, and at the bottom a single altar lamp still burning.

choices.text: Go down the steps into the river of stars

effects.log: Your avatar takes a breath you can feel in your own chest, and goes down.

choices.text: Map the ruin from the bank and come back for it

effects.log: It walks the bank until the stars turn, drawing every stone, and sleeps in the lee of a fallen pillar.

choices.text: Call it home before it is tempted

effects.log: You pull on the thread, gently. It turns from the river with a look you know: your own, when told no.

events.text: Your avatar has found a market held in the hollow of a dead star, open only while a comet passes. The traders are lesser gods with no domains left, and every lot is something a god once lost: a worshipper, a name, a season.

choices.text: Trade for the strangest thing in the hollow

effects.log: It trades a memory of yours you will not miss, and the trader wraps something heavy in black cloth.

choices.text: Only watch, and listen to the traders talk

effects.log: It sits at the rim until the comet goes, listening. The traders talk of domains, and it remembers every one.

choices.text: Leave before the comet takes the market away

effects.log: It steps out of the hollow as the comet turns, and the market goes with it.

events.text: A lesser god you have never met thanks you for the faith. Your clone {cf_clone} lent it in your name at a rate that would shame the Silent Hall, and has for an age. The ledger is in its hand, not yours.

choices.text: Confront it along the thread: you know

effects.log: It laughs, as if caught at a game. "Then I will play a different one," it says.

choices.text: Let it scheme, as long as the faith comes home

effects.log: The faith comes home. So does the feeling that you have been bought.

choices.text: Ask it what it would have, if it could have anything

effects.log: It tells you. It is less than you feared, and more than you can give.

events.text: On a night when no star of the Divine Realm is lit, the sky above your domain fills with what you were: thunder in a pool, the first wind of spring, an autumn blade, water under ice, a scale with no hand, the bamboo flowering, a ribbon coming home, the moon in every cup, the fire given away, the ground beneath all houses, the iron that learned to rest. Every one of them was once you. They turn around you like the sky around the pole star.

choices.text: Bow to all of them

effects.log: You bow, once to each, and each one bows back. It takes the whole night, and the gods who see it from their halls never speak of it to anyone.

choices.text: Ask them to teach you, all together

effects.log: They come closer. It is like standing in all the weather of every world at once.

choices.text: Ask them only to remember you

effects.log: "We are what remembers," says the thunder, and the fire, and the ground, together. "That is all we have ever been."

events.text: The seat has passed to you, and with it {elu_the}: gods of small things who were keeping its altars long before you came. {elu_m} has come to the steps of the temple with the token held out in one hand, not quite offering it. "We have done this before," {em_he} says. "We would like to know if you are going to be the sort who needs it explained."

choices.text: Ask {em_him} to explain it

effects.log: {em_He} considers this for some time. "That," {em_he} says, "is the right sort." It takes about nine years.

choices.text: Take the token, and give your first order

effects.log: It is a good order. They carry it out at once. It will be an age before you find out what they really thought.

events.text: Your cult is young and its altars are few, and the gods around your corner of heaven have noticed both. You call together the priests who came to you first, the ones who swept the steps before there were steps, and tell them that from today some of them will be {elu_name}. The eldest wants to know whether the name will be written in the Book of Fates. Of course it will. Everything is.

choices.text: Have it written in the Book, in full

effects.log: It takes eleven years for the clerks of the Heavenly Court to write it, which is quick up here. It is very handsome ink.

choices.text: Leave the Book out of it

effects.log: No clerk of the Court knows of them. The gods around you find this unsettling, as you hoped.

events.text: At the door of your temple, where the Star River runs past the steps, someone is sitting on the threshold as if they had been sitting there a long time: {npc}. {He} came through the light after you, asking every god the way. {He} stands up slowly. "You took your time," {he} says, and {his} voice breaks on the last word.

choices.text: Run the last steps

mem.note: ran up the last steps to me

effects.log: You run the last steps. {npc} catches you, and for a long while neither of you has anything to say at all.

choices.text: Ask {him} to show you how {he} found you

mem.note: showed me the road to them

effects.log: {npc} takes your hand and shows you the whole road: the river of stars, the domains that turned {him} away, the one god who pointed. {He} kept a list.

choices.text: Give back the promise you made

mem.note: kept the promise to follow

effects.log: "I said I would follow," you say. "You came anyway." {npc} laughs and cries at once, and the lesser gods nearby politely study the stars.

events.text: Someone is pacing up and down the steps of your temple the way {he} used to pace the courtyard before an exam: {npc}, your child, who climbed the clouds and then came on through the light to find you. {He} sees you and stops dead. "I kept a room for you," {he} says. "Up there, and now I will keep one here. You always liked a window."

choices.text: Hold {him} as you did when {he} was small

mem.note: was held at the door of the temple

effects.log: {npc} is taller than you remember, and an immortal, and it makes no difference at all. You hold on for a long time.

choices.text: Ask {him} to tell you of the road here

mem.note: kept a room for me among the gods

effects.log: {npc} tells you all of it, and everyone {he} has told about you on the way. It turns out to be most of the Divine Realm.

choices.text: Look at what {he} has become, and tell {him}

mem.note: saw what I had become among the gods

effects.log: You tell {npc} exactly what you see: someone who went further than you dared hope. {He} has to look away at the stars for a while.

events.text: On the edge of your domain a house stands that looks exactly like the one below: the same gate, the same plum tree, built from starlight by {npc}, your child, who came through the light after you, so that you would know it when you saw it. {He} opens the gate before you knock. "Welcome home," {he} says.

choices.text: Walk in and sit under the plum tree

mem.note: sat under the plum tree in the house of starlight

effects.log: You sit under the starlit plum tree with {npc}, and for an evening it is the old courtyard again, with all of heaven for a roof.

choices.text: Ask {him} how long {he} waited

mem.note: was asked how long I waited

effects.log: "Not long," {npc} says, which is plainly untrue. {He} has kept every year of it in a book by the gate.

events.text: Your disciple {npc} has come through the light to find you, older in the eyes and dressed like an immortal, and still bows the way you taught {him} at nine years old: too low, and too long. "Master," {he} says. "I kept a place for you, and then I had to come and find you."

choices.text: Raise {him} up and look at what {he} has become

mem.note: saw what I had become among the gods

effects.log: You raise {npc} up. {He} has grown strong on the road here, stronger than you knew. It is the best thing you have seen in an age.

choices.text: Ask {him} what {he} learned on the way

mem.note: asked me to show them the Divine Realm

effects.log: For once the student teaches the master. {npc} tells you which domains are kind to strangers and which gods to avoid, very seriously, and you let {him}.

events.text: An immortal in plain robes is waiting at the door of your temple, and the lesser gods make way for {him}: {npc}, your old master, who came through the light after you. "I counted the years," {npc} says. "And then I stopped counting and came."

choices.text: Bow as {his} student, as on the first day

mem.note: bowed to me as on the first day

effects.log: {npc} returns the bow, and then cuffs the back of your head, as {he} used to. "Never mind bowing. You are a god. Show me around."

choices.text: Ask {him} to teach you still

mem.note: asked to be taught again among the gods

effects.log: "A god asking to be taught," {npc} says, very pleased. "Good. You have a great deal to learn." {He} is right.

events.text: You feel it before you see it, in the middle of your own domain: a pressure you know as well as your own heartbeat. {npc} has come through the light after you and is leaning on a pillar of your temple, a realm above you, exactly as you expected. "So," your rival says. "The race goes on."

choices.text: Challenge {him} on the spot

mem.note: was challenged the moment they arrived

effects.log: You fight until the sky over your domain is in tatters. {npc} wins, of course, and offers you a hand up. "Not yet," {he} says. "But soon."

choices.text: Laugh, and shake {his} hand

mem.note: laughed and shook my hand among the gods

effects.log: You both laugh. Two old rivals in a heaven full of gods. It is good to see a face you know, even this one.

choices.text: Walk past and start training

effects.log: You walk past {npc} without a word and sit down to train. Behind you {he} laughs out loud. The race goes on.

choices.text: "I said I would catch you." Hold out your hand

mem.note: kept the vow shouted at the foot of the stairs

effects.log: {npc} looks at the hand, then at you, and takes it. "You did," {he} says. "Took you long enough." The race goes on, and it is better with two.

events.text: Among the gods at the Heavenly Court is a face the whole world below once knew: {npc}, who climbed into the sky while you were still a mortal, and came on through the light. {He} raises a cup to you. "Someone from home," {he} says.

choices.text: Sit with {him} and talk of the world below

mem.note: talked of home with me among the gods

effects.log: You talk of the world below until the stars turn beneath your feet. {npc} wants to know everything that happened after {he} left.

choices.text: Ask {him} what to beware of among the gods

mem.note: asked my counsel among the gods

effects.log: {npc} names three gods to avoid and one to trust. In the ages to come you will be very glad of all four names.

events.text: At the door of your temple {npc} is waiting with the crest of your house still sewn on {his} sleeve, a little faded from the long road through the light. "I told them all the way up who chose me," {he} says. "Half of them did not believe me. Come and show them."

choices.text: Go and show them

mem.note: was met again in the Divine Realm

effects.log: {npc} walks you through the halls of your own domain introducing you to everyone. You are, it turns out, a legend here too.

choices.text: Ask about the climb

mem.note: told the whole climb to the one who chose me

effects.log: {npc} tells you all of it, every realm and every fall, and the light at the end. It took {him} a very long time. {He} never once gave up.

choices.text: Look at the crest on {his} sleeve

mem.note: had the house crest straightened among the gods

effects.log: You straighten the faded crest. {npc} pretends not to be moved, and fails.

effects.log: {npc} tells you all of it, every realm and every fall, and the light at the end. It took {him} a very long time. {He} never once gave up.

mem.note: had the house crest straightened among the gods

effects.log: You straighten the faded crest. {npc} pretends not to be moved, and fails.

events.text: The tribulation gathers over the gate of {rgs_gate} and is only a tribulation: gold cloud, a wind off the Star River, the white crack of lightning between the domains. No faces. You look for them, half afraid. None. This life has left nobody in the heavens waiting for an answer.

choices.text: Give thanks for a clean heart

effects.log: You give thanks to nobody in particular. The storm seems almost to nod.

choices.text: Walk up into the weather

effects.log: You walk up into it like a farmer into spring rain. It is only weather.

events.text: A storm rolls across your domain and you stand out on the temple steps in it without meaning to, face to the sky, as if waiting for someone. No one comes. You have the strangest feeling that once many did, and that you forgave them all.

choices.text: Stand in the rain a while longer

effects.log: You stand there until you are soaked, and you feel lighter than you have in an age.

choices.text: Go back inside, smiling

effects.log: You go back inside, smiling at nothing. The rain keeps its secret.
